The '''Hida no Kuni no Miyatsuko''' ({{lang|ja|斐陀国造}}, also read ''Hida kokuzō'') were the {{ill|Kuni no miyatsuko|ja|国造|lt=kuni no miyatsuko|lt_ja=国造}} who ruled {{ill|Hida Province (ancient)|ja|斐陀国|lt=Hida|lt_ja=斐陀国}}. The name is also written {{lang|ja|斐太国造}} and {{lang|ja|飛騨国造}}.

== Overview ==
=== Name ===
The "Kokuzō Hongi" of the ''{{ill|Sendai Kuji Hongi|ja|先代旧事本紀|lt=Sendai Kuji Hongi|lt_ja=先代旧事本紀}}'' writes the name as '''{{lang|ja|斐陀国造}}'''; it is also written '''{{lang|ja|斐太国造}}''' and '''{{lang|ja|飛騨国造}}'''.

=== Ancestry ===
* According to the "Kokuzō Hongi" of the ''Sendai Kuji Hongi'', '''{{ill|Ōyahashi no Mikoto|ja|大八椅命|lt=Ōyahashi no Mikoto|lt_ja=大八椅命}}''', son of '''{{ill|Okitsuyosō|ja|瀛津世襲|lt=Okitsuyosō no Mikoto|lt_ja=瀛津世襲命}}''', was appointed Hida no Kuni no Miyatsuko in the reign of {{ill|Emperor Seimu|ja|成務天皇|lt=Emperor Seimu|lt_ja=成務朝}}.

=== Clan ===
The '''{{ill|Hida clan|ja|斐陀氏|lt=Hida clan|lt_ja=斐陀氏}}''' (ひだうじ), whose {{ill|Kabane|ja|カバネ|lt=kabane|lt_ja=姓}} was {{ill|Kuni no miyatsuko|ja|国造|lt=Kuni no Miyatsuko|lt_ja=国造}}; the family name was also written {{lang|ja|飛騨氏}} and {{lang|ja|斐陀氏}}. The '''Hida no {{ill|Sukune|ja|宿禰|lt=Sukune|lt_ja=宿禰}}''' ({{lang|ja|肥田宿禰}}) seen in the sources are thought to be its descendants. According to the "Kokuzō Hongi" and other sources, the Hida no Kuni no Miyatsuko were of the same line as the {{ill|Mononobe clan|ja|物部氏|lt=Mononobe|lt_ja=物部氏}} and the {{ill|Owari clan|ja|尾張氏|lt=Owari|lt_ja=尾張氏}}.

== Base ==
The seat of the ''kuni no miyatsuko'' is said to have been the '''{{ill|Furukawa Basin|ja|古川盆地|lt=Furukawa Basin|lt_ja=古川盆地}}''' and '''{{ill|Takayama Basin|ja|高山盆地|lt=Takayama Basin|lt_ja=高山盆地}}''' along the {{ill|Miya River (Gifu)|ja|宮川 (岐阜県)|lt=Miya River|lt_ja=宮川}}, the area running from {{ill|Furukawa, Gifu|ja|古川町|lt=Furukawa|lt_ja=古川町}} in {{ill|Hida, Gifu|ja|飛騨市|lt=Hida|lt_ja=飛騨市}} to northern {{ill|Takayama, Gifu|ja|高山市|lt=Takayama|lt_ja=高山市}}, where {{ill|Kokufu, Gifu|ja|国府町 (岐阜県)|lt=Kokufu|lt_ja=国府町}} lies, in present-day {{ill|Gifu Prefecture|ja|岐阜県|lt=Gifu Prefecture|lt_ja=岐阜県}}. From the distribution of kofun in particular, the centre is estimated to have been around Hirose in Kokufu and {{ill|Mikkamachi|ja|三日町|lt=Mikkamachi|lt_ja=三日町}}, in the south of the Furukawa Basin.<ref name="houga">{{ill|Takao Hōga|ja|宝賀寿男|lt=Hōga Toshio|lt_ja=宝賀寿男}}, "[http://wwr2.ucom.ne.jp/hetoyc15/kodaisi/ryoumen/ryoumen1.htm Ryōmen Sukuna and the Hida no Kuni no Miyatsuko]", ''Koju Kinobōma'', 2010.</ref>

=== Territory ===
The territory of the ''kuni no miyatsuko'' was the region then called '''Hida''', the whole of the later '''{{ill|Hida Province|ja|飛騨国|lt=Hida Province|lt_ja=飛騨国}}''': present-day {{ill|Takayama, Gifu|ja|高山市|lt=Takayama|lt_ja=高山市}}, {{ill|Hida, Gifu|ja|飛騨市|lt=Hida|lt_ja=飛騨市}}, {{ill|Gero, Gifu|ja|下呂市|lt=Gero|lt_ja=下呂市}} and {{ill|Shirakawa, Gifu|ja|白川村|lt=Shirakawa|lt_ja=白川村}} in {{ill|Gifu Prefecture|ja|岐阜県|lt=Gifu Prefecture|lt_ja=岐阜県}}.

== Clan deity ==
'''{{ill|Minashi Shrine|ja|飛騨一宮水無神社|lt=Hida Ichinomiya Minashi Shrine|lt_ja=飛騨一宮水無神社}}''' in {{ill|Takayama, Gifu|ja|高山市|lt=Takayama|lt_ja=高山市}}, the {{ill|Ichinomiya|ja|一宮|lt=ichinomiya|lt_ja=一宮}} of {{ill|Hida Province|ja|飛騨国|lt=Hida Province|lt_ja=飛騨国}}. One theory makes its deity, the Minashi god, another name for {{ill|Ōtoshi|ja|大年神|lt=Ōtoshi|lt_ja=大年神}}, {{ill|Sukunabikona|ja|少名毘古那神|lt=Sukunabikona|lt_ja=少名毘古那神}} or {{ill|Amenohoakari|ja|天火明命|lt=Amenohoakari|lt_ja=天火明命}}.{{citation needed|date=March 2022}} Another sees it as {{ill|Mizuhanome|ja|罔象女神|lt=Mizuhanome|lt_ja=罔象女神}}. The Ichinomiya family, who served the shrine until the {{ill|Middle Ages|ja|中世|lt=medieval period|lt_ja=中世}}, are thought to have been descendants of the ''kuni no miyatsuko''.{{citation needed|date=March 2022}}

=== Related shrines ===
* {{ill|Hida Sōja|ja|飛騨総社|lt=Hida Sōja|lt_ja=飛騨総社}} (ひだそうしゃ)
*: The {{ill|Sōja shrine|ja|総社|lt=sōja|lt_ja=総社}} of Hida Province, in Takayama, Gifu Prefecture.
* {{ill|Takada Shrine (Hida)|ja|高田神社 (飛騨市)|lt=Takada Shrine|lt_ja=高田神社}} (たかだじんじゃ)
*: A shrine in Furukawa, {{ill|Hida, Gifu|ja|飛騨市|lt=Hida|lt_ja=飛騨市}}, enshrining {{ill|Kamo-wakeikazuchi|ja|賀茂別雷命|lt=Kamo-wakeikazuchi|lt_ja=鴨別雷命}} and {{ill|Amatsuhikone|ja|天津彦根命|lt=Amatsuhikone|lt_ja=天津彦根命}}.
* {{ill|Araki Shrine|ja|荒城神社|lt=Araki Shrine|lt_ja=荒城神社}} (あらきじんじゃ)
*: By one account it enshrines Ōaraki no Mikoto, which suggests a link with the Hida no Kuni no Miyatsuko.<ref name="houga"/>
* {{ill|Atayuta Shrine|ja|阿多由太神社|lt=Atayuta Shrine|lt_ja=阿多由太神社}} (あたゆたじんじゃ)
*: A shrine in Kokufu, Takayama, enshrining the {{ill|Kumano deities|ja|熊野神|lt=Kumano deity|lt_ja=熊野神}}.
* {{ill|Kurihara Shrine|ja|栗原神社|lt=Kurihara Shrine|lt_ja=栗原神社}} (くりはらじんじゃ)
*: A shrine in {{ill|Kamitakara, Gifu|ja|上宝町|lt=Kamitakara|lt_ja=上宝町}}, Takayama, enshrining {{ill|Isotakeru|ja|五十猛神|lt=Isotakeru|lt_ja=五十猛神}}.
* {{ill|Tachigao Shrine|ja|剱緒神社|lt=Tachigao Shrine|lt_ja=剱緒神社}} (たちがおじんじゃ)
*: A shrine in Kokufu, Takayama, said to have been founded by the ''kuni no miyatsuko''.

== Descendants ==
* {{ill|Hida no Takechimaro|ja|飛騨高市麻呂|lt=Hida no Takechimaro|lt_ja=飛騨高市麻呂}}
*: A {{ill|Nara period|ja|奈良時代|lt=Nara-period|lt_ja=奈良時代}} magnate; {{ill|Dairyō|ja|大領|lt=district governor|lt_ja=大領}} of {{ill|Ōno District, Gifu|ja|大野郡 (岐阜県)|lt=Ōno District|lt_ja=大野郡}}, Hida Province, of {{ill|Junior Fifth Rank|ja|従五位|lt=Junior Fifth Rank|lt_ja=従五位}}, Lower Grade; judge in the office for building {{ill|Saidai-ji|ja|西大寺 (奈良市)|lt=Saidai-ji|lt_ja=西大寺}}.
* {{ill|Hida no Iwakatsu|ja|飛騨石勝|lt=Hida no Iwakatsu|lt_ja=飛騨石勝}}
*: A Nara-period official; senior recorder in the Ministry of Civil Affairs, of {{ill|Junior Sixth Rank|ja|従六位|lt=Junior Sixth Rank|lt_ja=従六位}}, Lower Grade.
* {{ill|Hida no Sokado|ja|飛騨祖門|lt=Hida no Sokado|lt_ja=飛騨祖門}}
*: An official of the Nara and Heian periods. Of {{ill|Junior Seventh Rank|ja|従七位|lt=Junior Seventh Rank|lt_ja=従七位}}, Lower Grade, he was appointed Hida no Kuni no Miyatsuko; assistant in the Bureau of Accounts and the Bureau of Taxation.
